item.title: US Time Change Rekindles Daylight Saving Debate
item.description: Clocks will skip ahead an hour at 2 a.m. Sunday for daylight saving time in most of the United States, creating a 23-hour day that throws off sleep schedules, plunges early-morning dog walks into darkness, and inspires millions of complaints. Even though polls show many people dislike the system that has most Americans changing clocks twice a year, the political moves necessary to change the system haven't succeeded because opinions on the issue and its potential impacts are sharply divided. item.title: Lippo Group Donates 30 Hectares for Affordable Housing Project Near Jakarta
item.description: Bekasi. Indonesian conglomerate Lippo Group has donated 30 hectares of land to the government for the development of affordable housing for low-income families, a project that could provide up to 140,000 apartment units, officials said. The land is located in South Cikarang, Bekasi, east of Jakarta. item.title: China, Indonesia Beef Up Maritime Ties
item.description: Jakarta. The Chinese government has had “in-depth” maritime talks with Indonesia, according to its top diplomat, as Beijing and ASEAN seek to secure the “golden rules” for the coveted South China Sea within this year. ASEAN has long been pushing for a “code of conduct” on the South China Sea to avoid conflict in the strategic waterway. item.title: JCI Sinks 5.45% in Early Trading as Oil Tops $100 and Global Markets Reel from War Fears
item.description: Jakarta. Jakarta Composite Index (JCI) plunged sharply at Monday’s opening, tumbling 5.45% or 414 points to 7,174 within the first 15 minutes of trading, as escalating geopolitical tensions in the Middle East and surging oil prices triggered a global risk-off sentiment. The index had already dropped to 7,374 at the open before extending losses minutes later. item.title: Indonesia’s Budget Deficit to Near 4% of GDP if Oil Prices Top $100
item.description: Jakarta. An analyst recently warned that war-induced oil price hikes would cause Indonesia's budget shortfall to widen to almost 4% of the gross domestic product (GDP), thereby breaching its legal cap. The US-Israeli strike against Iran has triggered closure risks of the Strait of Hormuz, which handles 20% of the global oil shipments. item.title: Bali Prepares Special Rules as Eid Eve and Nyepi May Fall on Same Day
item.description: Bali. The Indonesian government has issued guidelines for Eid eve celebrations in Bali, where the Muslim tradition of takbiran parades may coincide with Nyepi, the Hindu Day of Silence observed across the island. Eid al-Fitr celebrations typically begin with takbiran, when Muslims gather to chant praises to God, often accompanied by drum processions and community parades on the night before the holiday. item.title: When Import Permits Stall, Industry Suffers
item.description: In discussions about trade balances, national independence and economic sovereignty are often simplified as reducing — or even eliminating — imports. Yet such an approach overlooks an important reality: imports are often essential components of domestic production. Import restrictions therefore must be implemented selectively. item.title: Antam Gold Drops Sharply as Global Prices Fall Over 1%
item.description: Jakarta. Antam gold prices tumbled sharply on Monday as global bullion weakened, with the benchmark one-gram bar dropping Rp 55,000 to Rp 3,004,000 ($176.86) per gram, according to data from Logam Mulia. The decline erased part of last week’s gains, when Antam gold had surged Rp 35,000 to Rp 3,059,000 per gram on Friday. Despite the drop, Antam gold remains significantly higher this year. Prices have climbed about 20% since the start of 2026, when bullion stood at Rp 2,488,000 per gram on Jan. 1

item.title: Japan Prepares for Deployment of Its First Home-Developed Long-Range Missile
item.description: Tokyo. Japan is preparing to deploy its first batch of domestically developed long-range missiles, with their launchers arriving at an army camp on Monday, as the country accelerates its offensive capability in response to rising regional challenges. The upgraded Type-12 land-to-ship missiles will be deployed at Camp Kengun in Japan’s southwestern prefecture of Kumamoto by the end of March, completing the process of deployment, Chief Cabinet Secretary Minoru Kihara said without giving details. item.title: Chandra Asri Raises MTBE, Butene-1 Plant Capacity to Cut Import
item.description: Jakarta. Southeast Asian chemical giant Chandra Asri Group announced Monday that it had raised its Methyl Tert-Butyl Ether (MTBE) and Butene-1 (B1) plant capacity by up to 25%. The company expects the move to help Indonesia cut imports of the said materials, thereby improving foreign exchange efficiency.
